definitions.explanation: An imitation or simulation of something real, done for practice or testing purposes.

examples.japanese: {模擬|もぎ}{試験|しけん}を{受|う}けた。
{模擬|もぎ}{裁判|さいばん}で{弁護士|べんごし}{役|やく}を{担当|たんとう}した。
examples.english: I played the role of lawyer in a mock trial.

examples.japanese: {文化祭|ぶんかさい}で{模擬|もぎ}{店|てん}を{出|だ}すことになった。
examples.english: We decided to set up a booth at the school festival.

notes:
Used as a prefix meaning mock, simulated, or practice. Almost always appears as the first element of a compound rather than standing alone.

COMPOUNDS:
- {模擬|もぎ}{試験|しけん} ({模試|もし}) — practice exam, mock test
- {模擬|もぎ}{裁判|さいばん} — mock trial
- {模擬|もぎ}{店|てん} — booth, stall (at a school festival)
- {模擬|もぎ}{戦|せん} — mock battle, war game
- {模擬|もぎ}{面接|めんせつ} — mock interview

USAGE:
The abbreviated form {模試|もし} (from {模擬|もぎ}{試験|しけん}) is extremely common among students preparing for entrance exams. {模擬|もぎ}{店|てん} is a staple of Japanese school festivals ({文化祭|ぶんかさい}), where student groups run temporary food stalls and game booths.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- シミュレーション — simulation (loanword, often technical)
- {練習|れんしゅう} — practice (general, not necessarily simulating something real)
